newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firm on inflation, auction hopes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firm on inflation, auction hopes.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed firmer for the second day in a row on Tuesday amid positive market forecasts for inflation data and the primary Cetes auction, traders said.
"The market was liquid (in dollars) and calm while awaiting mild inflation data and an uptick in Cetes rates," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 0.7 and 0.5 of a centavo firmer, respectively, at 7.9330/7.9360 and 7.9300/7.9340 per dollar.
Banco de Mexico was expected to release inflation data for the first half of June shortly after the close of trade in the foreign exchange market.
The latest Reuters survey MEX22 of 13 financial houses showed they forecast an average rise of 0.47 percent in the consumer price index during June 1-15.
Nine money market traders surveyed by Reuters shortly before bidding closed showed they expected the central bank to assign bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at an average of 20.50 percent.
This would be an increase of 46 basis points since last week.
Banco de Mexico was expected to announce auction results at 1830 local time/2330 GMT.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 3.6 centavos firmer at 7.9330/7.9380 per dollar.
